findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has dead code and always returns false
Error message misleads users about feature status
findings.body: The error returned to users is `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. This wording is misleading: SQL expressions are implemented (the package exists, the parser, command, and DB stubs are all wired up); the feature has been deliberately disabled as a security mitigation for CVE-2024-9264. A user (or operator) reading this error would conclude the functionality was never built rather than that it is currently turned off for safety. Consider something like `"sqlExpressions are disabled for security reasons (CVE-2024-9264)"` so the situation is clear and operators can grep for the CVE in their dashboards/logs.

findings.title: Alternate construction path for SQLCommand is not gated
findings.body: `NewSQLCommand` and the exported `UnmarshalSQLCommand` in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` are still publicly callable and do not consult the `enableSqlExpressions` feature check that was added in `pkg/expr/reader.go`. They rely on `sql.TablesList` failing because the new `DB` stub returns `"not implemented"`, which surfaces as the generic `errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql", ...)` with the public message `"error reading SQL command"`. This is inconsistent with the more specific `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"` produced from the reader path, and it means any caller that bypasses `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` gets a different (and less informative) error. The disablement should be enforced at a single chokepoint (or both paths should return the same clear message) so the security state is consistent regardless of entry point.

findings.title: No tests for the security mitigation
findings.body:
The PR is a security fix that disables the entire SQL Expressions feature, replacing the `go-duck` backend with stubs and adding a feature-gated branch in `ReadQuery`. There are no new tests verifying:
- that `ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` now returns the expected error,
- that `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` methods all return `"not implemented"`,
- that `NewSQLCommand` / `UnmarshalSQLCommand` no longer succeed.

For a CVE-driven fix, regression tests pinning the disabled behaviour are essential so that a future re-enable cannot accidentally land without an explicit test change.
